To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the right middle superior temporal gyrus plays an important role, and the left superior temporal gyrus is also involved, in the perception of speech intonation and rhythm.
the right middle superior temporal gyrus (STG) and the right superior temporal sulcus (STS) play a role in prosody processing.
speech rhythm and intonation are processed in different neural networks, and the right mSTGs is involved in prosodic processing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural basis of speech perception.
the neural mechanisms underlying the perception of speech prosody.
how humans perceive the prosodic aspects of speech.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the right mSTS plays a critical role in the processing of speech rhythm and intonation.
the right middle superior temporal gyrus (mSTS) plays an impor- tant role in the processing of both rhythmic and intonational prosody.
rhythm is a universal feature of language, and that the perception of rhythm is a fundamental aspect of speech perception.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the right middle superior temporal gyrus (mstg) is a common region for the perception of both speech rhythm and intonation.
speech rhythm is a perceptual phenomenon, whereas speech intonation is a linguistic phenomenon, which is supported by both neuroimaging and behavioral studies (e.g., [1–4]).
speech rhythm is processed in a right hemisphere dominant fashion and that speech intonation is processed in a bilateral fashion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rhythm and inton- ation activate different neural regions.
the brain regions involved in the perception of speech intonation and speech rhythm are largely overlapping, with the right superior temporal gyrus playing a central role.
the perception of prosodic features is supported by a network of brain regions that are also recruited for the perception of linguistic content.
